svg.title: RATE LIMITER: sketchnote
svg.text: Every public API needs one, and the obvious implementation has a race condition.
Counting per server gives each client N times its
limit; the counter must be shared, usually in Redis.
Read-then-write on a shared counter races. Do
the refill, check and decrement atomically in one
Decide what happens when Redis is down: allow
Limit requests per client (user, IP, API key) by
Return 429 with Retry-After and rate-limit headers
1M req/s = 1M Redis ops/s; one Redis node
does ~100k ops/s, so a ~10–20 shard Redis
Naive: each API server counts in local memory. With 50 servers,
Centralize counters in Redis. But GET then SET from
two servers races: both see 99/100 and both allow.
A Lua script runs refill + check + decrement atomically
inside single-threaded Redis, in one round trip, with no
Rules come from a config store cached in each
gateway. Decide failure mode: fail-open for normal
APIs, fail-closed for login and payments.
Token bucket (capacity = burst, refill = sustained rate) is the industry default.
Read-modify-write is a lost update (DDIA Ch 7). Atomic Lua or INCR + EXPIRE inside
Fall back to local limits (limit ÷ N servers). Fail-open vs fail-closed is a product decision
One key lands on one shard. Give each server a local allowance and sync periodically,
